scope: World-class prose intelligence gap research using public metadata/abstracts and professional standards only; no bulk copyrighted article/book body acquisition and no named-author imitation target.

method.freshness: Current literature was searched through 2026-09-09, with special attention to 2025-2026 evidence.
method.rights_boundary: Only public webpages, abstracts, bibliographic metadata, and short research summaries were used. No corpus body was ingested into the repository.
method.decision_rule: External research creates or hardens a capability requirement only when it survives comparison against existing Literary Prose contracts and does not weaken preservation, rights, author-intent, or human-authority boundaries.

sources.title: Professional Editorial Standards: Structural Editing
sources.key_evidence: Structural editing evaluates organization/content for audience, medium and purpose; it covers narrative flow, gaps, repetition, focus, accuracy and fiction anachronisms.
sources.repo_implication: Developmental/structural intelligence must remain purpose- and audience-conditioned and distinguish query/recommendation authority from automatic mutation.

sources.title: Professional Editorial Standards: Stylistic Editing
sources.key_evidence: Stylistic editing addresses clarity, coherence, flow, paragraph/sentence construction and language while maintaining voice, style, POV, tone, register and author goals.
sources.repo_implication: The existing preservation-first line-editing architecture is directionally correct; edit-scope authorization and author-goal conditioning must remain hard constraints.

sources.title: Professional Editorial Standards: Proofreading
sources.key_evidence: Proofreading requires checking requested changes for newly introduced problems and forbids drifting into structural/stylistic tasks without authorization.
sources.repo_implication: Revision verification should explicitly test collateral regressions and preserve stage/scope boundaries rather than rewarding broad unsolicited rewriting.

sources.title: Perspective - Point of View
sources.key_evidence: Narrative perspective is relational and may differ across spatial, ideological, temporal, linguistic and perceptual parameters; narrator voice and perspective/focalization should not be collapsed.
sources.repo_implication: POV checking should model narrator, focalizer, epistemic privilege, language/register and perspective shifts separately instead of treating POV as grammatical person.

sources.title: Focalization
sources.key_evidence: Focalization is selection/restriction of narrative information relative to narrator/character experience and knowledge.
sources.repo_implication: Knowledge-access violations need a first-class focalization/epistemic state model, not only local POV labels.

sources.title: Time
sources.key_evidence: Narrative theory distinguishes story time, discourse time and narrating time; order, duration and temporal relations are structural narrative variables.
sources.repo_implication: A canonical story-time/discourse-time authority is still needed; chapter-level pace statistics do not substitute for temporal order/duration/frequency representation.

sources.title: AI writing assistants shrink linguistic diversity and blur personal identity
sources.key_evidence: Research across 880,000 texts reports meaning-preserving AI assistance can compress linguistic variety and shift inferred personal traits.
sources.repo_implication: Anti-homogenization must measure identity-bearing style distributions across revisions/books, not merely semantic preservation.

sources.title: LitBench: A Benchmark and Dataset for Reliable Evaluation of Creative Writing
sources.key_evidence: The strongest tested off-the-shelf zero-shot judge reached only 73% agreement with human creative-writing preferences; specialized reward models reached 78%.
sources.repo_implication: Literary evaluation cannot treat a single generic LLM judge as authoritative; specialized calibration, human evidence and disagreement handling remain necessary.

sources.title: LitVISTA: A Benchmark for Narrative Orchestration in Literary Text
sources.key_evidence: Frontier models struggle to jointly capture narrative function and structure and to form an integrated global view; anchor identification/localization dominate failures.
sources.repo_implication: Whole-book intelligence needs explicit event/function anchors and orchestration state, not only aggregated chapter/arc statistics.

sources.title: Lost in Stories: Consistency Bugs in Long Story Generation by LLMs
sources.key_evidence: Long-story consistency errors are especially common in factual and temporal dimensions, cluster around narrative middles and co-occur across error types.
sources.repo_implication: Canonical entity/event/causal/temporal state and middle-book regression probes are high-value missing controls.

sources.title: Style over Story: Measuring LLM Narrative Preferences via Structured Selection
sources.key_evidence: Across six LLMs and narratology-grounded constraints, models consistently preferred Style over Event, Character and Setting content elements.
sources.repo_implication: Opportunity admission/evaluation must prevent attractive surface-style changes from outranking story-function, character, event and setting requirements.

sources.title: Rethinking Creativity Evaluation: A Critical Analysis of Existing Creativity Evaluations
sources.key_evidence: Creativity metrics disagree across domains; perplexity, LLM judging, lexical-diversity measures and syntactic-template measures each have domain-specific failure modes.
sources.repo_implication: No universal creativity/prose score should be introduced; creativity evidence must remain multidimensional, task-conditioned and human-calibrated.

sources.title: Creativity Bias: How Machine Evaluation Struggles with Creativity in Literary Translations
sources.key_evidence: Automatic metrics and LLM judges correlated poorly with professional creativity judgments and penalized creative/culturally appropriate solutions, especially in more literary genres.
sources.repo_implication: Unusual but intentional language must have explicit protection and evaluation cannot infer defect from deviation from routine phrasing.

sources.title: PersonaForge: Psychology-Grounded Dual-Process Architecture for Personality-Consistent Role-Playing Agents
sources.key_evidence: Explicit multidimensional personality constraints reduced long-interaction personality drift in controlled role-playing experiments.
sources.repo_implication: Character state should be durable and multidimensional across long-form spans; prose-level voice alone is not sufficient for character consistency.

sources.title: Contrastive Decoding Mitigates Score Range Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
sources.key_evidence: LLM judge outputs can be sensitive to the predefined scoring range.
sources.repo_implication: Literary evaluator outputs should prefer pairwise/ordinal decisions and explicit evidence over arbitrary scalar ranges.

sources.title: Prior Beliefs Prejudice LLM-as-Judge: Evidence from Persuasion Evaluation
sources.key_evidence: LLM judges can conflate alignment-instilled beliefs with rhetorical quality despite task instructions.
sources.repo_implication: Theological/philosophical/rhetorical evaluation needs content-belief separation and human escalation when value commitments affect literary judgment.

sources.title: Rating Roulette: Self-Inconsistency in LLM-As-A-Judge Frameworks
sources.key_evidence: LLM judges show low intra-rater reliability across repeated evaluations.
sources.repo_implication: Repeated model judgments require stability measurement; correlated reruns are not independent votes.

sources.title: Arbiters of Ambivalence: Challenges of using LLMs in No-Consensus tasks
sources.key_evidence: LLMs used as judges tend to force a stance in ambivalent/no-consensus settings and do not fully represent human non-agreement.
sources.repo_implication: REVIEW_CONFLICT/abstention must be first-class outcomes rather than forced ranking.

sources.title: Are LLM-Judges Robust to Expressions of Uncertainty?
sources.key_evidence: All tested judges showed negative bias toward epistemic markers, particularly uncertainty markers.
sources.repo_implication: Uncertainty wording must not itself become negative literary evidence; evaluator robustness fixtures should test uncertainty-preserving paraphrases.

sources.title: Beyond the Surface: Measuring Self-Preference in LLM Judgments
sources.key_evidence: LLM judges can favor their own responses; style and post-training data influence the effect.
sources.repo_implication: Generator identity must be blinded from the evaluator when practical and cannot count as evidence.

sources.title: Towards A Novel Benchmark: Evaluating Literary Fiction with Large Language Models
sources.key_evidence: Long-form fiction evaluation benefits from separate macro, meso and micro levels; human evaluation exposed a high-starting/low-ending pattern in LLM fiction.
sources.repo_implication: Whole-book evaluation must remain multi-resolution and include ending/closure regression rather than extrapolating from local quality.

sources.title: STORYTELLER: An Enhanced Plot-Planning Framework for Coherent and Cohesive Story Generation
sources.key_evidence: A narrative entity knowledge graph plus event/plot nodes improved long-form coherence in the reported experiments.
sources.repo_implication: The existing gap for a canonical manuscript entity-event-causal state graph is externally reinforced.

sources.title: Generating Long-form Story Using Dynamic Hierarchical Outlining with Memory-Enhancement
sources.key_evidence: Temporal knowledge graphs and a temporal conflict analyzer improved reported long-story consistency/coherence.
sources.repo_implication: Story-time state and temporal-conflict checks should become durable whole-book evidence.

sources.title: Metaphor and Large Language Models: When Surface Features Matter More than Deep Understanding
sources.key_evidence: LLM metaphor performance can be driven by lexical overlap and sentence length rather than robust figurative understanding.
sources.repo_implication: Imagery/metaphor diagnosis should test contextual function and interpretation, not rely on detection labels or surface novelty.

sources.title: A Theoretical Framework for Evaluating Narrative Surprise in Large Language Models
sources.publisher: Workshop on Narrative Understanding / ACL Anthology
sources.key_evidence: Narrative surprise depends on multiple factors including predictability and post-dictability/retrospective coherence; human-authored endings retained an advantage in the tested mysteries.
sources.repo_implication: Surprise/payoff should be assessed as setup-to-payoff structure, not raw unpredictability.

sources.title: Narrative transportation: A systematic literature review and future research agenda
sources.key_evidence: A systematic review of 95 peer-reviewed articles distinguishes narrative transportation from related constructs and highlights storyteller, recipient and medium antecedents.
sources.repo_implication: Reader-experience modeling should keep immersion/transportation distinct from generic engagement or prose fluency.
